_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: a jump of 1.5 at the cut-off

agreement.claim: both engines report the same estimate, bandwidths, conventional and robust intervals
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0. harness/quasi_examples.test.py refits the local linear regression by hand with a triangular kernel at rdrobust's bandwidth (agreeing to 1e-8, with the same counts inside h), requires the robust interval to be wider than the conventional one, and the global straight-line jump to miss by more than 0.5.

recovery.claim: the estimates are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: A first fixture used a symmetric curvature (x squared), which biases both sides equally and cancels in the jump; the negative control could not fire. It now uses x cubed. Measured by harness/quasi_examples.test.py, running python.py on seeds 0 to 99.
